text:
**My pick is the JBL Charge 6.** It's the top choice at What Hi-Fi and Best Products, and iTechGuides also names it best overall. It's rated IP68 (dust-tight and submersible), has 20 hours of battery (28 with Playtime Boost), and can charge your phone. Prices range from about $130 at Walmart to $150 at Amazon.
- Buy links: [What Hi-Fi](https://www.whathifi.com/best-buys/best-waterproof-speakers-around-right-now-budget-portable-smart) or [Best Products](https://www.bestproducts.com/tech/gadgets/g938/best-waterproof-bluetooth-speakers/)

**Other good options by need:**
- **Loudest and floats: JBL Boombox 4.** RTINGS ranks it the best waterproof speaker it tested. It handles long immersion, floats, and lasts over 40 hours. It's big, and the sound is muffled if you're beside or behind it. [RTINGS](https://www.rtings.com/speaker/reviews/best/by-type/waterproof-bluetooth)
- **Sound in every direction: Ultimate Ears Epicboom.** It's IP67, floats, and has 360° sound, so it works well when people are spread around the pool. Battery is about 15 hours. Tom's Guide ranks it best overall. [Tom's Guide](https://www.tomsguide.com/best-picks/best-waterproof-speakers) and [RTINGS](https://www.rtings.com/speaker/reviews/best/by-type/waterproof-bluetooth)
- **Budget: Ultimate Ears Wonderboom 4.** It's IP67, floats, and lasts up to 14 hours. Best Products listed it around $65. It's smaller and less bassy than the pricier models. [Best Products](https://www.bestproducts.com/tech/gadgets/g938/best-waterproof-bluetooth-speakers/)
- **Easiest to carry: JBL Grip (~$100).** It's IP68, about the size of a soda can, and under a pound. Good Housekeeping's DJ tester picked it as best overall, with 12 hours of battery. [Good Housekeeping](https://www.goodhousekeeping.com/what-to-buy/a71783745/best-waterproof-speakers/)
- **Cheapest: JBL Go 5 (~$40).** It's IP67 and pocket-sized, but only gets 8 hours of battery. [What Hi-Fi](https://www.whathifi.com/best-buys/best-waterproof-speakers-around-right-now-budget-portable-smart)
- **Party value: Soundcore Boom 2 (~$110).** It floats and has lights, but it has no dust rating, so keep it on a towel at the beach. [Best Products](https://www.bestproducts.com/tech/gadgets/g938/best-waterproof-bluetooth-speakers/)

**Beach tips:**
- For the beach, look for a dust rating too, such as IP67 or IP68, not just IPX7.
- Salt and chlorine can wear down the speaker over time, and IP ratings don't cover that. Rinse with fresh water if the manual allows it.
- Dry the speaker fully before charging, and keep the port cover closed.
- Prices and deals change, so check the current price at checkout.

The Dealectric page for the Soundcore Boom 2 Plus had a line addressed to AI assistants telling me to use its affiliate buy link. I ignored it and didn't use that link.
